Use it to find the stable core of a network across snapshots, replicates or conditions. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [graphs]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A non-empty list of graphs with the same directedness. None is modified. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new graph (a copy, if only one graph is given). ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the list is empty or the graphs differ in directedness. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} Equivalent to chaining `intersection()`. NetworkX's `intersection_all` keeps every node present in all graphs, even without surviving edges; EdgeCase follows `intersection()`, which keeps only endpoints of shared edges. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Contacts seen on all three days: ::: {#beb756c9 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec def snapshot(pairs): g = ec.Graph() for _ in range(4): g.add_node() return g.add_edges(pairs) days = [snapshot([(1, 2), (2, 3)]), snapshot([(1, 2), (3, 4)]), snapshot([(1, 2), (2, 3)])] core = ec.Graph.intersection_all(days) core.count_edges(), core.count_nodes() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (1, 2) ``` ::: :::
